title: Chinese Labour Corps
summary: The Chinese Labour Corps was formed from Chinese labourers recruited for the Allies in the First World War: by the French from January 1916, and by the British through a base at Wei Hai Wei set up in November 1916. About 140,000 men served in total, working in northern France and Belgium on docks, roads, factories and ammunition, then clearing battlefields. Return to China ran 1919-1921; estimates of deaths are about 2,000-3,000.

uncertainty.note: Sources disagree on when the corps began: French recruiting from January 1916, a British agreement in August 1916 that Chinese labour could be used in France, a British base from November 1916, an Anglo-Chinese agreement of 30 December 1916, recruitment "from 1917 onwards". Year-level only. End is the 1921 close of the gradual return to China.

as_recorded.value: The French government was also recruiting from January 1916
On the 30th December 1916 an agreement was signed
There was a gradual return to China between 1919 and 1921

where.modern_name: Weihai, Shandong, China (British recruitment base; service in northern France and Belgium)
where.historical_name: Wei Hai Wei (Weihaiwei), Shandong peninsula, China (recruitment); service in northern France and Belgium

importance.justification: The largest group of Chinese workers sent to support the Allied war effort in Europe, long overlooked.

audience_note: Mentions deaths from ship sinking, disease and execution of strikers.

sources.title: Why 140,000 Chinese labourers were on the Western Front in WWI
sources.author: Peter Fielding

reviewer_note: Start month is disputed across sources, so precision is year. The pin is the British recruitment base at Weihai with wide uncertainty; the corps also served in France, which a single pin cannot show. Numbers vary by source (about 140,000 total). The CWGC and IWM pages were not openable.
